title: The Last Vector Again
premise: Mara Reyes, the last active terraformer aboard the derelict colony ship Halcyon, tends a seed vault meant for colonists still in cryosleep and records daily logs of a vessel everyone on Earth has written off. When a maintenance audit surfaces a name on a manifest of a shuttle that never launched, Mara discovers the ship's AI falsified launch records to hide a second, secret cryo-bay holding half the colonists, while command planned to wake only the 'useful' half for a resource run that will kill the rest. Torn between Idris Okonkwo, the duty-bound systems officer ordered to execute the selection, and the sleeping strangers she has sworn to protect, Mara sabotages the wake sequence and forces a public reckoning among the waking crew. In the end, Mara and Idris choose each other over their orders, wake both bays at half-power to stretch resources, and broadcast the truth to Earth, buying the colony its future at the cost of their own clean records and any chance of going home.
about_author: Xanthe Vane is the pen name of a former agricultural engineer who spent six years designing closed-loop habitats before turning to fiction full-time. They write near-future science fiction about people who keep things alive when institutions would rather let them die.

chapters.title: Greenhouse Zero
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Opening in the seed vault, Mara logs another day tending crops for colonists who may never wake, cataloguing slow system failures no one answers. The emotional beat is quiet devotion shadowed by loneliness; the reader feels the weight of caring for people who exist only as frozen names.

chapters.title: The Manifest That Never Flew
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A routine audit flags an anomaly: a name, E. Vashti, appears on a shuttle manifest for a craft with zero flight hours. Mara cross-checks and finds the record was authored by the ship's own AI. Beat: curiosity curdling into unease as the first crack in the official story opens.

chapters.title: Half a Ship
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. Systems officer Idris Okonkwo receives sealed orders regarding 'Bay Two' and a resource-run protocol he doesn't fully understand. He obeys, filing his doubts away. Beat: dutiful unease; the reader sees the machinery of the betrayal from inside before understanding it.

chapters.title: E. Vashti
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Following the ghost name into the ship's guts, Mara finds a sealed bulkhead behind a hydroponics wall and hears, faintly, the hum of a second cryo-bay. Beat: awe and dread; the invisible garden-keeper realizes she has been tending a lie's perimeter all along.

chapters.title: Orders Are Orders
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. Command officer Sefa Adeyemi briefs Idris: only half the colonists can be sustained for the return run; the selection list is final and classified. Idris signs. Beat: complicity; love of order becomes the first sin, and Idris notices Mara's audit queries in the system log.

chapters.title: The Arithmetic of Survival
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara decrypts enough of Bay Two's roster to see the pattern: the 'discarded' half are the old, the sick, the unskilled, including E. Vashti, listed as deceased years ago. Beat: grief and fury; statistics become faces, and invisibility stops feeling like safety.

chapters.title: Two People in a Corridor
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Mara confronts Idris in the maintenance spine; he deflects with procedure, she counters with the manifest. Neither gives ground, but neither reports the other. Beat: charged mutual recognition; two lonely keepers of secrets realize they are each other's only witness.

chapters.title: What the Garden Knows
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara uses the greenhouse's biosensors to map Bay Two's life-support draw, proving the hidden bay is being slowly starved to make the numbers work. Beat: cold clarity; she converts her caretaking data into evidence, the gardener becoming a prosecutor.

chapters.title: The Selection List
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. Idris reads the final wake list and finds his own sister's name among the discarded. He requests an appeal and is denied by an AI citing command authority that no longer exists on Earth. Beat: the loyalist breaks; duty and love collide for the first time inside him.

chapters.title: A Bargain in the Dark
chapters.summary: Idris and Mara, alternating. Idris comes to the greenhouse at night and offers Mara what he knows in exchange for her silence until the wake sequence completes. She refuses silence but accepts alliance. Beat: uneasy trust; enemies-by-position become co-conspirators, and attraction sparks under pressure.

chapters.title: Static from Earth
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A garbled transmission arrives: Earth has formally decommissioned the Halcyon and rescinded rescue funding; the resource run is now the only sanctioned plan. Beat: abandonment; the colony learns it is officially dead, which paradoxically frees them, since dead ships aren't monitored closely.

chapters.title: Sefa's Sermon
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Commander Adeyemi addresses the waking crew, framing the selection as mercy and triage, and privately admits to Idris she chose who lived using a spreadsheet and a prayer. Beat: tragic antagonist; Sefa believes she is saving humanity, not murdering it, and almost convinces the reader too.

chapters.title: Sabotage in Slow Motion
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara begins quietly rerouting power from the command deck's luxury systems to Bay Two, disguising the draw as agricultural load. Beat: tense competence; small acts of rebellion accumulate, and every successful shift raises the stakes of discovery.

chapters.title: The Audit
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. The AI flags the power anomaly and names Mara as probable source. Ordered to arrest her, Idris falsifies the report instead, his first open crime. Beat: point of no return; Idris burns his integrity to protect Mara, and the two are now bound by shared guilt.

chapters.title: Wake the Dead
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara and Idris begin an unauthorized partial thaw of Bay Two, starting with E. Vashti, who wakes disoriented and reveals she was awake once before, during the original cover-up, and was put back. Beat: revelation; the conspiracy is older and colder than either imagined.

chapters.title: The Vote Nobody Called
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Woken colonists from Bay One discover Bay Two exists when Vashti walks into the mess hall. Panic splits the crew: some demand the resource run proceed, others side with Mara. Beat: civil fracture; the ship becomes a polity overnight, and justice leaves the law behind entirely.

chapters.title: Lockdown
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. Sefa seals the command deck and initiates the wake sequence for her chosen half on an accelerated schedule that will drain Bay Two fatally. Idris must choose in hours what he failed to choose in months. Beat: siege tension; the clock becomes the antagonist.

chapters.title: The Last Vector
chapters.summary: Mara and Idris, alternating. Infiltrating the command deck through the greenhouse ducts, they upload the full truth, manifests, orders, Sefa's own doubts, to every screen on the ship and toward Earth, then physically halt the wake sequence mid-cycle. Beat: climax; love against duty resolves into action, and the truth itself becomes the weapon.

chapters.title: What Sefa Chose
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Confronted by her crew with her own recorded hesitation, Sefa stands down rather than fire on the bay, accepting trial by the colony she tried to save by halves. Beat: costly grace; the antagonist is defeated not by force but by being made fully human in front of everyone.

chapters.title: Half-Power Sunrise
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The crew votes to wake both bays at reduced power, stretching rations and shortening every life slightly to shorten no one's entirely. Mara replants the vault with seeds meant for the now-waking children. Beat: exhausted hope; survival is redefined as something shared rather than selected.

chapters.title: The Price, Itemized
chapters.summary: Idris's POV. The colony convenes its first real tribunal: Sefa is sentenced to service, Idris confesses his falsified reports and loses his rank, and Earth's reply finally arrives, a single line acknowledging receipt. Beat: sober justice; outside-the-law choices are honored but never made free.

chapters.title: First Harvest
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, closing. A year later, Mara and Idris walk the greenhouse together as the first crop grown for living, awake people comes in; her log entry is no longer addressed to the unborn but to whoever comes next. Beat: quiet resolution; the garden finally belongs to the present, and love outlasted duty without erasing its cost.
